Third case in the embolism series: here the exercise is to find the thrombus in the left lung, which hides in the lower lobe artery behind the bronchus, and not to mistake epicardial fat for a pericardial effusion (measure the density with the ROI: fat about −100 HU, fluid 0-20 HU). The thrombus on the right is more evident, but the report must list all sites.

As in the other cases: after the thrombi, the right heart is measured (RV/LV ratio, septum, reflux into the cava) and the critical finding is communicated immediately.
